lists the places where passing is not allowed. Start with a rule about the edge of the road. You may never pass on the right by leaving the paved or main part of the roadway. Each rule stands on its own, so a pass must clear all of them. Passing is forbidden where your lane is bordered by a double solid line or by a solid dividing line on your side. So before you pull out to pass, look at the line on your side of the road. A solid line there, or a double solid line, ends the question. The other rules in this lesson still apply even when the line is broken. Read the line before every pass, because it can change along the road. In short: Double solid line: no passing; solid line on your side: no passing; broken line on your side: check others.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Curves and hilltops","fact_ids":["sec07-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Cannot see far enough ahead.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03"]},{"text":"Do not pass near a curve.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03"]},{"text":"Do not pass near a hilltop.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Some places forbid passing because of what you cannot see. Do not pass when approaching a curve or a hilltop where you cannot see far enough ahead to know passing is safe. A curve or the crest of a hill can hide an oncoming vehicle until it is too late, which is exactly the situation the manual rules out. If you cannot see far enough ahead to know a pass is safe, you do not pass. If you are unsure whether you can see far enough, the answer is to wait. In short: Cannot see far enough ahead; do not pass near a curve; do not pass near a hilltop.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Two separate reasons","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"A solid line forbids passing.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]},{"text":"A hidden road forbids passing.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]},{"text":"Either one is enough.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. So check both: the line on your side, and whether you can see far enough ahead. In short: A solid line forbids passing; A hidden road forbids passing; either one is enough. Remember: Passing is forbidden where your lane is bordered by a double solid line or by a solid dividing line on your side.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Crossings, bridges and tunnels","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-F05","sec07-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Street and railroad crossings.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-F05","sec07-R01"]},{"text":"View-blocking bridges, tunnels, underpasses.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-F05","sec07-R01"]},{"text":"One hundred feet for each.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-F05","sec07-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here are the places with a set distance. The manual ties them together. Street crossings, railroad crossings and view-blocking bridges, tunnels or underpasses all share one no-passing distance of one hundred feet. In short: Street and railroad crossings; view-blocking bridges, tunnels, underpasses; one hundred feet for each.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-F05","sec07-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the distance","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R01","sec07-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"A tunnel blocks your view ahead.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R01","sec07-F04"]},{"text":"How close may you pass?","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R01","sec07-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a tunnel ahead blocks your view of the road. Street crossings, railroad crossings and view-blocking bridges, tunnels or underpasses all share one no-passing distance of one hundred feet. One number for all of these places makes it easy to remember. Do not pass within one hundred feet of a street crossing or a railroad crossing, or of a bridge, tunnel or underpass that blocks your view. Each condition is enough on its own to rule out a pass. In short: Stay on the pavement; solid lines and hidden roads; one hundred feet from crossings and tunnels.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05","sec07-R01","sec07-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec07-u02","module_id":"sec07-m02","objective_ids":["sec07-u02"],"title":{"text":"Driving a roundabout","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F08","sec07-F07"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Roundabouts keep traffic moving, but only when every driver yields correctly and keeps a steady, slow speed.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F09","sec07-F11"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Mia approaches a roundabout and has picked her exit.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10"]},"reasoning":{"text":"She slows down, yields to cars already circling and to a bicyclist in the crosswalk, and enters on a gap.","fact_ids":["sec07-F11","sec07-F09","sec07-F07"]},"result":{"text":"Inside she keeps moving, and when she misses her street she simply goes around again.","fact_ids":["sec07-F12","sec07-F13"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking you should stop inside the roundabout if you are unsure of your exit.","fact_ids":["sec07-R04"]},"correction":{"text":"The design speed is an approach speed; Here is what one is. A roundabout is a circular intersection where traffic moves almost nonstop in one direction around a central island. Traffic always moves the same way around the island. Always enter a roundabout to the right of its central island. In the slides ahead we cover whom you yield to, choosing your lane, the right speed, entering and moving through, and what to do if you miss your exit. In short: A circular intersection; one direction around an island; almost nonstop traffic.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Who goes first","fact_ids":["sec07-F14","sec07-F09","sec07-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Vehicles inside have the right-of-way.","fact_ids":["sec07-F14","sec07-F09","sec07-F07"]},{"text":"Yield when arriving.","fact_ids":["sec07-F14","sec07-F09","sec07-F07"]},{"text":"Yield to large vehicles entering.","fact_ids":["sec07-F14","sec07-F09","sec07-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Right-of-way at a roundabout is simple. Vehicles already in the roundabout have the right-of-way. So the duty falls on drivers arriving. Drivers arriving at a roundabout must yield to every vehicle already circulating and to large vehicles entering at the same moment. Pedestrians and bicyclists come into the picture too. At a roundabout, always yield to pedestrians and bicyclists who are crossing the road. Yielding is what lets traffic inside keep moving almost nonstop. In short: Vehicles inside have the right-of-way; yield when arriving; yield to large vehicles entering.","fact_ids":["sec07-F14","sec07-F09","sec07-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Yield to more than cars","fact_ids":["sec07-R03","sec07-F09","sec07-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Circulating traffic.","fact_ids":["sec07-R03","sec07-F09","sec07-F07"]},{"text":"Large vehicles entering with you.","fact_ids":["sec07-R03","sec07-F09","sec07-F07"]},{"text":"Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.","fact_ids":["sec07-R03","sec07-F09","sec07-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a common slip. In short: Circulating traffic; large vehicles entering with you; pedestrians and bicyclists crossing. You may leave a roundabout at any street, and if you miss your exit you can simply go around again. Going around again is always an option. Decide your exit early and move into the right lane. Slow to the design speed of fifteen to twenty miles per hour, enter on a gap, never stop inside, and go around again if you miss your exit.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-F11","sec07-F12","sec07-F13","sec07-F14","sec07-R03","sec07-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec07-u03","module_id":"sec07-m03","objective_ids":["sec07-u03"],"title":{"text":"Roundabout special cases","fact_ids":["sec07-F15","sec07-F16","sec07-R05"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Trucks, emergency vehicles, pedestrians and bicyclists each need special care in a roundabout.","fact_ids":["sec07-F15","sec07-F16","sec07-F17"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Leo is circling a roundabout when he hears a siren and sees an emergency vehicle behind him.","fact_ids":["sec07-F16"]},"reasoning":{"text":"His exit is the next street, so he proceeds carefully and exits.","fact_ids":["sec07-F16","sec07-R05"]},"result":{"text":"If he could not exit, he would pull over to the right instead.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking you should stop immediately inside a roundabout for an emergency vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05"]},"correction":{"text":"The manual says to proceed with caution and exit if you can, and only otherwise pull over to the right.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F16"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Siren in the circle: exit first.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"An emergency vehicle appears while you are in a roundabout and you can reach your exit. Exit first if you can; pull over to the right only if you cannot, and in both cases keep moving carefully. Keep it calm and careful. In short: Proceed carefully; exit if you can; otherwise pull over to the right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Exit before pulling over","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Do not stop in the circle.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F16"]},{"text":"Exit first if possible.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F16"]},{"text":"Pull right only if you cannot.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. In short: Do not stop in the circle; exit first if possible; pull right only if you cannot. In short: Pedestrians use crosswalks with caution; bicyclists follow traffic rules; or walk the bike across. Remember: At a roundabout, always yield to pedestrians and bicyclists who are crossing the road.","fact_ids":["sec07-F17","sec07-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":32,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the emergency rule","fact_ids":["sec07-F16","sec07-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Emergency vehicle behind you.","fact_ids":["sec07-F16","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"Your exit is next.","fact_ids":["sec07-F16","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"What do you do?","fact_ids":["sec07-F16","sec07-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: you are in a roundabout, an emergency vehicle appears, and your exit is the next street. What should you do? The answer is to proceed carefully and exit. If you see an emergency vehicle while in a roundabout, proceed carefully and exit if you can, or else pull over to the right.
